memos.scout:
The strongest honest case here is thin, and I don't think it clears the bar.

What the brief does show: the coin is alive, the last 15 minutes carried about 31.5 SOL of buys from 149 buyers against 15.5 SOL of sells from 16 sellers, net flow is positive, and the pool is deep at roughly 5,089 SOL, so a $20 ticket would see little impact. Price is up 2.1% over 30 minutes with no drawdown from the high.

But the same brief shows the demand is concentrated. Post-graduation, 5,002 SOL came from 22 buyers, the top 5 accounted for essentially all of it, and a launch bot is present. The curve shows bundle share at 1.0 and top-3 share at 1.0. Recent flow, while positive, is a small fraction of what the operators already put in, and the 149 buyers are a count, not evidence of broad demand. A market cap of $175M after 30 minutes on a bundled launch is the kind of number that is set by one or two wallets.

No real demand case survives this. The recent buying could persist for 30-60 minutes, but the exit liquidity is held by a handful of operators who can exit at will, and the base rates for this class are roughly break-even before our 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost. The honest scout call is to skip.
memos.skeptic:
Most likely loss: insider distribution after a bundled launch. The brief shows bundle_share 1.0 and top3_share 1.0, with 22 buyers in the first two minutes absorbing 5,002 SOL, and top5 buyers holding 99.99% of early buys. That concentration means a handful of wallets control nearly all supply, and a launch bot was present. Their cost basis is far below the current price, so they can sell into our $20 bid at any time.

Recent flow already leans toward exit: over the last 15 minutes, sell_sol (15.53) is nearly half of buy_sol (31.5), with 16 sellers against 149 buyers. Fees of 1.4-5.1% plus impact on a 5,088 SOL pool won't be the main drag. A single insider unload would be.

The 2.1% 30-minute return and 0% drawdown look calm but reflect no real price discovery. Skip.
